I, Yahweh, the first, and with the last, I am he.”, pointed מִֽי פָעַ֣ל וְעָשָׂ֔ה קֹרֵ֥א הַדֹּר֖וֹת מֵרֹ֑אשׁ אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ רִאשׁ֔וֹן וְאֶת אַחֲרֹנִ֖ים אֲנִי הֽוּא (oshb:Isa.41.4, tier: byte). The closing vignette at web:Isa.41.7 reads, So the carpenter encourages the goldsmith. He who smooths with the hammer encourages him who strikes the anvil, saying of the soldering, “It is good;” and he fastens it with nails, that it might not totter., pointed וַיְחַזֵּ֤ק חָרָשׁ֙ אֶת צֹרֵ֔ף מַחֲלִ֥יק פַּטִּ֖ישׁ אֶת ה֣וֹלֶם פָּ֑עַם אֹמֵ֤ר לַדֶּ֨בֶק֙ ט֣וֹב ה֔וּא וַיְחַזְּקֵ֥הוּ בְמַסְמְרִ֖ים לֹ֥א יִמּֽוֹט (oshb:Isa.41.7, tier: byte). The judicial-summons idiom opening this span at web:Isa.41.1 recurs in a related but distinct form later in this same part at web:Isa.41.21: יִגְּשׁוּ֙ and נִקְרָֽבָה (oshb:Isa.41.1, tier: byte) stand against קָרְב֥וּ and הַגִּ֨ישׁוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.41.21, tier: byte), each byte tier against its own verse, the same two roots in inverted order — the draw-near root by contiguous skeleton (sweep: 3 verses, chs 40-41) and the bring-near root per attested spelling, defective here (sweep: 1 verse) against the plene form later (sweep: 2 verses) — disclosed here as a rival architecture bracketing the fear-not oracle between them rather than treating the two spans as one unit.
